sentiment.reason_it: Il sentiment di mercato è risk-off a causa dell'aumento del VIX (+6.78%) e della chiusura in calo degli indici azionari (S&P 500 -1.24%). Il DXY è salito (+0.39%) e il prezzo del petrolio è aumentato (+3.35%).
sentiment.reason_en: Market sentiment is risk-off due to the increase in VIX (+6.78%) and the decline in equity indices (S&P 500 -1.24%). The DXY rose (+0.39%) and oil prices increased (+3.35%).

market_impact_summary.en: The previous close saw an increase in VIX and a decline in equity indices. The DXY rose and oil prices increased. Interest rates rose (US 10Y Yield +3.00%).

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert. 


Mentre i mercati tradizionali sono chiusi per il fine settimana, analizziamo la situazione attuale. 
Nella seduta di nella seduta precedente, il Nikkei ha chiuso in calo dell'1.99%, Shanghai in calo dell'1.02%. 
Questo suggerisce un'apertura debole per i mercati europei se fossero aperti.


Sul fronte dei mercati occidentali, nella chiusura passata, S&P 500 in calo dell'1.24%, VIX in rialzo del 6.78%, 
DXY in aumento dello 0.39%, oro in calo del 2.61% a 4555.8 dollari l'oncia, 
petrolio in rialzo del 3.35% a 109.26 dollari, US 10Y Yield in aumento del 3% al 4.59%. 
Il BTP 10Y è a 3.73%.


Nessun evento geopolitico di rilievo oggi, ma la situazione in Iran e le tensioni globali restano monitorate.


Sul fronte macro, nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi.


Passando agli asset digitali, che operano 24/7, Bitcoin è in calo dello 0.82% a 78,421 dollari. 
Restiamo in attesa per ulteriori sviluppi nel comparto crypto.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin mostra una direzione negativa, con una variazione del -2,95%, scendendo sotto gli ottantamila dollari. I flussi ETF hanno registrato una uscita di 12,2 milioni di dollari. Questo movimento potrebbe essere influenzato da notizie recenti come il deposito di Bitcoin Depot che ha gettato ombre sul futuro della società a causa di procedimenti giudiziari. Inoltre, una strategia di riacquisto di obbligazioni convertibili del valore di 1,5 miliardi di dollari, utilizzando contanti o vendite di bitcoin, potrebbe avere un impatto sul mercato. 

  Tra le altcoin, Ethereum registra un -3,21%, scendendo a duemilatrecento dollari, Solana perde il -4,72% a ottantasette dollari e ventiquattro centesimi, mentre BNB mostra un calo del -3,68%, arrivando a seicentocinquantanove dollari e cinquantasette centesimi.

  Il Fear & Greed Index è a 31, in zona Fear, suggerisce cautela sugli investitori.

Sui mercati attendiamo i dati economici in uscita oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en:
Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. 

While traditional markets are closed for the weekend, let's analyze the current situation. 
In the previous session, the Nikkei closed down 1.99%, Shanghai down 1.02%. 
This suggests a weak opening for European markets if they were open.

On the Western market front, in the previous close, S&P 500 down 1.24%, VIX up 6.78%, 
DXY up 0.39%, gold down 2.61% to $4,555.8 per ounce, 
oil up 3.35% to $109.26, US 10Y Yield up 3% to 4.59%. 
The 10Y BTP is at 3.73%.

No major geopolitical events today, but the situation in Iran and global tensions remain monitored.

On the macro front, no major economic data releases today.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets, which operate 24/7 Bitcoin is down 0.82% to $78,421 
We are waiting for further developments in the crypto sector.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin shows a negative direction, with a variation of -2.95%, falling below eighty thousand dollars. ETF flows have recorded an outflow of $12.2 million. This movement could be influenced by recent news such as the filing of Bitcoin Depot, which has cast shadows on the company's future due to legal proceedings. Furthermore, a convertible bond buyback strategy worth $1.5 billion, using cash or bitcoin sales, could have an impact on the market. 

Among altcoins, Ethereum is down 3.21% to $2,300, Solana loses 4.72% to $87.24, while BNB shows a decline of 3.68% to $659.57

The Fear & Greed Index is at 31, in Fear zone, suggesting caution among investors.

We are awaiting economic data releases today. To delve deeper into today's topics, find the full articles in the Top Stories section on our platform. Thank you for your attention, and we'll see you tomorrow.

articles.title: Hormuz crisis could lead to constructive dialogue between ASEAN and China in the South China Sea
articles.snippet: Hormuz crisis could lead to constructive dialogue between ASEAN and China in the South China Sea Expert comment LToremark 15 May 2026 Oil shortages as a result of the Iran war present a unique opportunity for ASEAN chair the Philippines to make progress on a South China Sea Code of Conduct with China. And for Trump to strike a deal. The crisis in the Middle East is being felt deeply in Southeast Asia. Perhaps most of all in the Philippines, which imports 98 per cent of its oil from the Gulf. The choking of global oil trade has led to acute fuel shortages, causing the Philippine government to declare a national emergency. The situation has forced President Ferdinand Marcos Jr to consider all options, even with the most unlikely of partners – China. Chaos opens door to dialogue Relations bet

articles.title: The Trump-Xi summit: What does the US want from China and will Trump get it? Independent Thinking podcast
articles.snippet: The Trump-Xi summit: What does the US want from China and will Trump get it? Independent Thinking podcast Audio sseth.drupal@c… 15 May 2026 Our experts analyse the two superpowers’ aims as President Trump meets President Xi Jinping in Beijing. President Donald Trump brings a band of senior US business executives seeking trade deals to China for what is possibly the biggest bilateral summit of 2026. But what does the US hope to achieve? More sales of Boeings, beef and soybeans; an off-ramp from the US-Israel war on Iran; a sense of world pre-eminence; or all three? articles.title: How to Win a Trade War: Book launch and discussion with Bown and Keynes
articles.snippet: Soumaya Keynes and Chad P. Bown discuss their new book How to Win a Trade War, available for pre-order. Trade wars are here to stay, and refusing to engage in the fight is no longer an option. President Donald Trump's tariff announcements can crash markets and sour decades-long alliances. China's export restrictions on rare earths could bring the West's car production to a crashing halt. Curbs on trade in cutting-edge chips could determine who wins the artificial intelligence (AI) race. From identifying supply chain vulnerabilities to installing stockpiles, subsidies, and trade restrictions,…

articles.title: South Korea’s 500,000 Drone Warriors Will Be a Hollow Force
articles.snippet: Ukraine has reshaped the battlefield with cheap, expendable drones. South Korea reads the signals and wants to match the scale. North Korea has been reading the same signals through a more direct channel. Since late 2024, North Korea has rotated thousands of troops through Russia’s war in Ukraine, alongside what is currently the world’s most combat tested drone force — tied with Ukraine’s, of course. articles.title: India Signs LPG and Strategic Oil Reserves Deal with UAE
articles.snippet: India on Friday signed a strategic agreement with the United Arab Emirates to receive liquefied petroleum gas from the UAE, as well as a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on strategic petroleum reserves. India, which uses LPG as its the main cooking fuel and has felt shortages since the Iran war choked supplies at the Strait of Hormuz, seeks to boost its supply agreements. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi signed the LPG supply deal and the strategic reserves pact during a quick two-hour visit to the UAE today, as India scrambles to ease energy…

articles.title: Oil Prices Surge as Hormuz Shutdown Keeps Supply Fears Alive
articles.snippet: Crude oil prices rallied hard this week as traders focused on the growing supply threat tied to the U.S.-Iran conflict. July WTI crude oil futures settled Thursday at $97.91, gaining $6.79, or 7.45%, for the week. Prices traded in a wide range between $92.84 and $99.09 as the market reacted to war headlines, tighter inventories, and inflation concerns.
